gaps.note: UfiSpace has published no hardware installation guide for the S9620 family - the intake's own coverage sheet records the miss for all three S9620 models - so this device is modelled from a datasheet and two product renders and nothing else. Everything a guide normally supplies is therefore absent here: no faceplate figure with numbered callouts, so no callout audit was possible and any feature the render does not show is not merely unmodelled but unknown; no front-panel or FRU LED table, so no lamp on this device carries a state vocabulary; no component dimension table, so the fan and PSU faces are the library's from a sibling platform; no rear elevation; no rail or grounding section. This is the single largest limitation on the model and every other gap here descends from it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC Hardware Installation Guide, when UfiSpace publishes it

gaps.note: The largest front image UfiSpace serves is 520 x 150 px, which is 1.125 px/mm and 0.89 mm per pixel. Every size token on the product page was probed (/image/5e/, /image/5g/ and eighteen others) and nothing larger exists; the datasheet's own copy of the same picture is 158 px native. The render passes Gate 1 on aspect (9.900 against 10.000) so its PROPORTIONS are trustworthy and the standard pitches confirm them across 24 columns to 0.3 mm - but no printed legend on this faceplate is legible, no connector keyway is readable, and every coordinate quoted here to a tenth is really good to about half a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of a real S9620-54DC faceplate at 2000 px or better

gaps.note: The datasheet lists a 100/1000M RJ-45 management port, an RJ45 serial console port and a USB 3.0 Type-A port. NONE OF THE THREE IS ON THE FRONT FACE - the front render shows exactly one RJ45, inside the timing block, and no USB opening anywhere, and the whole left block is only 24 mm wide. They are therefore on the rear, which UfiSpace publishes no image of. So three documented ports exist on this device and are modelled nowhere, and the mgmt group is not declared at all rather than being declared empty.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: No rear image of this model exists - the vendor publishes a front and a 45-degree front angle and nothing else, and there is no installation guide. The inventory is sourced (five hot-swap fans in a 4+1 set, two hot-swap 750 W supplies in a 1+1 set, all exhaust, front-to-back) but EVERY REAR COORDINATE IN THIS FILE IS INVENTED: the 52.0 mm fan pitch, the x 12.0 start, the supplies at the right, the vertical centring. They are laid out the way the library's other UfiSpace 1RU boxes are laid out, which is a plausible arrangement and not this chassis's. Nothing else is drawn on that face for the same reason.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of an S9620-54DC, or the hardware installation guide

gaps.note: The tile at x 78.2-105.5 carries six lamps - four green across the top, one green and one blue below - and a printed legend beside each. At 1.125 px/mm those legends are two pixels tall and cannot be read, so NO legend is printed in this drawing and the lamps carry positional ids. The arrangement is the S7801-54XS's exactly (four lamps with a blue ID lamp beneath the fourth), whose HIG names them SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and ID, and the extra green lamp under the first is where a timing platform's SYNC lamp sits on the S9610-36D. That reading is recorded here so the next reader has it; it is not written into the artwork, and no lamp carries a state vocabulary because no LED table exists for this platform.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's front-panel LED table, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The faceplate prints port numerals on the yellow, teal and blue bands - two glyph clusters per column are visible - and this render cannot resolve a single digit. The numerals drawn are reconstructed as 0-53 left to right, even on the top row and odd on the bottom, which is what every UfiSpace box in this library does and what the per-column up/down lamp pair implies. Two things are genuinely open: whether UfiSpace numbers the 400G pair first on this SKU rather than last, and whether the run starts at 0 or 1. The olive band under the four 100G ports carries no printing at all, so those four are drawn unlabelled.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: PORTS 48-51 ARE DRAWN WITHOUT NUMERALS ON PURPOSE, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY FOUR OF FIFTY-FOUR THAT ARE. The olive band under the two 100G QSFP-DD columns carries no printing: crop the three bands side by side at 26x and the teal band to its left is packed with dark glyph clusters, two per column, while the olive band holds a white up-triangle at each end, a white down-triangle at each end, eight round lamps along its lower edge and nothing else, and the steel-blue band to its right carries light glyphs at both ends. The blue band is the control that makes this a reading rather than a resolution artefact: it is the same darkness as the olive one and its printing survives, so a legend on the olive band would have survived too. Numerically the olive band's upper half (rows y 91-93 px) is uniform where the teal and blue bands vary. The vent strip above the shell was checked as well and carries only the lamp row and its two triangles. So this faceplate appears to identify its 100G pair by band colour and row triangle rather than by number. Printing 48-51 would put ink on the drawing that is not on the metal, which is the one thing silkscreen must never do - so they are left off, and this entry exists so that a reader comparing the render against the photograph can tell a deliberate absence from an unfinished model. If a legible photograph ever shows numerals there, they belong on the band in the light fill the blue band uses, which is what is legible on an olive ground.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph, or the HIG's port map

gaps.note: The silver strip between the upper and lower cage rows on all three QSFP-DD shells is FINELY MARKED, not blank, and this render cannot separate the marks. Rows y 73-78 px read 190 / 84 / 152 / 130 / 96 / 186, so there are two darker rows at 21.1 and 23.8 mm inside a lighter band - that much is solid, and it is what the drawing reproduces, as decor. What it will not do is name a count. A local-minimum scan finds a 4.44 mm rhythm, but the two 100G columns - which are identical hardware - put that rhythm at offsets 1.7/6.2/10.6/15.1 mm in one column and 4.1/8.5/13.0/17.4 in the next, asymmetric in opposite directions and disagreeing by 2.4 mm. Two identical columns cannot really differ; that is the signature of sampling a pattern finer than the pixel grid, and the residual darkness between the minima says the true pitch is about half, near 2.2 mm, which 0.89 mm per pixel cannot resolve. So it is not decided whether these are indicators or the ganged cage's gasket comb. Against them being lamps: each 100G port already carries four round lamps that DO resolve, four above the shell and four on the olive band below it, so strip lamps would give one port twelve indicators; and the pattern continues across the 400G column, which has no lamp row above it at all. Nothing is drawn as an LED here on that reasoning, and no lane count is asserted in either direction.
gaps.wanted: a faceplate photograph at 2000 px or better, or the HIG's port-LED figure

gaps.note: Two identical 8.0 mm SMB jacks sit at (29.3, 5.3) and (44.4, 5.3) with a printed legend beside each that this render cannot read. They are assigned 10MHz and 1PPS in the order the datasheet's Timing Interfaces row lists them, which is a convention, not a reading - and the S9610-36D prints its pair the other way up in a vertical stack, so there is no house order to fall back on either. The GNSS SMA is identified independently, by being the larger connector and the only SMA the datasheet lists.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: The ToD RJ45's latch direction cannot be determined: the opening is eleven pixels across and the notch that would settle it is one. The jack is drawn in std/rj45-ganged's own orientation. On a single jack this is cosmetic; it is recorded because the library has been caught by mirrored stacked pairs before and the check was genuinely run here rather than skipped.
gaps.wanted: a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: Each of the twenty-four SFP columns carries two small dark 1.8 mm squares on the silver inter-row strip, at 2.7 and 12.0 mm from the column edge, flanking the up/down lamp pair - 48 of them, counted. They are drawn as decor because nothing identifies them: they could be a second lamp per port drawn unlit, a shell fastener or a gasket feature, and with no LED table and no faceplate figure there is no way to choose. Drawing them as lamps would assert a per-port indicator this device may not have.
gaps.wanted: the HIG's front-panel figure, or a legible faceplate photograph

gaps.note: No document held states what any port lamp means. The geometry is read: one up-triangle and one down-triangle per SFP column, four round lamps above and four below each 100G QSFP-DD column, and two lamps below the 400G column with none above it. The last of those is measured rather than assumed - the vent perforation runs unbroken above the 400G shell where it is visibly interrupted above the 100G shell - but whether the 400G pair really has one lamp each, or a lane row this render cannot separate, is open. Every lamp keeps its component's plain off/on default. The strip between the two QSFP-DD rows is finely marked rather than blank and is drawn as a banded decor field of the measured tone; its marks could not be separated and are deliberately not modelled as lamps. See the qsfp-inter-row-marks gap, which carries the measurement that decides it.
gaps.wanted: the S9620-54DC HIG's LED tables, or a NOS LED reference

gaps.note: This datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow'. The library has ufispace/fan-405637, built from the S9110-32X's guide, at 50.7 x 40.0 mm. One digit apart in a number that encodes the rotor, so the two are probably one family and possibly not one face. There is no S9620-54DC guide to measure the real module against and no image of it, so the component is reused with its model attribute overridden to FAN-405636-HD and the substitution recorded here rather than hidden. If the faces differ, five bays on the rear are the wrong width.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide, or the S9620-54DC HIG's component table

gaps.note: No wattage for the fan module appears anywhere. The datasheet's Fan Types line reads 'FAN-405636-HD, exhaust air flow' with no figure beside it, and there is no installation guide to carry a component table. Both datasheet pages were searched at 200 dpi for every occurrence of 'W', 'Watt' and 'power': the only hits are the two PSU ordering lines (750W), the AC/DC input ratings and the single system figure (125 W typical, no transceiver). The L29 warning this device carries is therefore left standing, and the modelled module total is a floor rather than a total.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace FAN-405636 specification, or a measured figure from a live unit

gaps.note: This datasheet orders PSU-751-AESR-1C and PSU-751-DESR-1C; the library's psu-751 components were drawn for the S9110-32X, which orders PSU-751-AESR and -DESR at the same 750 W and the same input ranges. The '-1C' suffix is undocumented in any held file. The faces are assumed identical and the model attribute is overridden per configuration.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power-supply ordering guide

gaps.note: Both supplies are orderable and no held image shows either one seated, because there is no rear image. The base configuration seats the DC unit, which is an arbitrary choice recorded as arbitrary - on the S9610-36D the same choice was settled by reading a terminal block out of the rear elevation, and here there is nothing to read.

gaps.note: The angle render shows the left side face carrying a column of countersunk ear-mount holes near the front and a run of rail features along its length, and the lid carrying three long transverse stiffening ribs and a scatter of fastener dimples. The counts are read off that render at 45 degrees; NOT ONE POSITION IS DIMENSIONED ANYWHERE, so every coordinate on the four non-port faces is estimated and evenly spread. gaps.note: Three features on the left block are drawn because two independent images put them there and are not named, because with no guide there is no callout list to name them with: a 4.4 mm round icon at (72.4, 5.7) carrying a diamond-shaped glyph, between the model legend and the lamp tile, and two 2.7 mm dark circles at (6.2, 37.4) and (16.9, 37.4) under the ToD jack. A third, the 2.7 mm circle at (6.2, 14.5), is placed as common/reset-button on the reading that a recessed pinhole above a management jack is a reset - which every other UfiSpace box in this library has - and that reading is a guess too.

provenance.attrs: datasheet - the Physical, Environmental, Performance and Regulatory Compliance tables and the Supported Accessories block, read off a 200 dpi page render because the text is outlined. Compliance strings kept verbatim and semicolon-separated.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - '1RU, 440.0 mm(W) x 480.0 mm(D) x 44 mm(H) or 17.32" x 18.89" x 1.73"', 'Weight: 10.76 kg (without FRU)'. 440 is the body, not a rack face: it is 17.32 inches, and the render draws two small bracket tabs standing outside the full-height body on each side (px 8-13 against a body of 14-508), which are the mounting hardware and are not drawn. No document states the ear extent or the handle projection, because there is no installation guide.
provenance.front-layout: photo-measured at 1.125 / 1.136 px/mm, quoted to 0.1 mm because that is what the arithmetic gives and NOT because the image resolves it - one pixel is 0.89 mm, so every front coordinate here is good to about +/-0.5 mm and no better. Left to right: the timing block (GNSS SMA, two SMB jacks, a reset pinhole, the model legend, an unnamed round icon, the six-lamp status tile, and one RJ45 in a bright bezel with two small unidentified circles under it), then twenty-four ganged SFP columns in two twelve-column shells, then two 100G QSFP-DD columns and one 400G QSFP-DD column.
provenance.gate-1: the front render PASSES and it is the only thing here that does. Body measures 495 x 50 px (x 14-508, y 50-99) against the datasheet's 440 x 44 mm: aspect 9.900 against a true 10.000, 1.0% out, so it is orthographic and reads at 1.1250 px/mm across and 1.1364 down. It is also TINY. 520 x 150 px is the largest image UfiSpace serves - /image/5e/ and /image/5g/ were probed against every other size token on the product page and nothing above 650 px exists - so one pixel is 0.89 mm and no legend on this faceplate is legible. The datasheet's own 'Front and Back Views' strip is the same raster at 158 px native and shows the FRONT only; there is no back view in it despite the caption. The angle render (650 x 278) is a 45-degree view and fails Gate 1 outright; it is used for construction, counts and colour, never for a dimension.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9620-54DC end of life' - no announcement found. The vendor's aggregation-router product page and the datasheet (revision 20260811V01) are both live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.
provenance.panel-decor: photo-measured. The perforated vent field above the ports runs x 108.4-433.8 at y 1.8-8.8 (it starts where the lamp tile ends, not at the chassis edge), and a second perforated row runs x 24.0-367.1 at y 40.5-43.1 - under the SFP block only, stopping where the QSFP shells begin, which is measured rather than tidied. The silver ganged-cage shells are drawn as decor behind the ports, per the S9510-28DC and S7801-54XS precedent: without them a dark cage on a dark faceplate is invisible. Band colours are the peak pixel of each band, not its mean, because the printed glyphs and lamps drag the mean down.
provenance.part-numbers: The datasheet's Available to Order block names PSU-751-AESR-1C and PSU-751-DESR-1C; the library's ufispace/psu-751-ac and -dc were drawn for the S9110-32X, which orders PSU-751-AESR and -DESR at the same 750 W on the same 50.5 x 40.2 face. The base configuration overrides the model attribute to this product's own -1C spelling. The fan is worse: this datasheet says FAN-405636-HD and the library's component is FAN-405637-HD from the S9110-32X, one digit apart in a number that encodes the rotor, so it is probably the same face and possibly not. It is reused with the model overridden and the disagreement filed rather than resolved. Neither part's face was re-measured here, because there is no guide to measure it against.
provenance.port-leds: photo-measured. Each SFP column carries ONE UP-TRIANGLE AND ONE DOWN-TRIANGLE on the silver inter-row strip - 48 green marks counted by colour, exactly two per column, at x offsets 5.8 and 9.3 mm from the column edge and y 22.0-23.8 mm. Up names the top-row port and down the bottom, the arrangement the S9510-28DC HIG figure documents and the S7801-54XS reuses. They sit 3.56 mm apart, so common/led-arrow (3.6 mm wide) COLLIDES and common/led-arrow-sm (2.25) is used instead: the right pitch in a smaller shape. Flanking each pair are two small dark squares, 1.8 mm, at offsets 2.7 and 12.0 mm - 48 of those as well. They are drawn as decor because nothing identifies them and a dark square is not a lamp shape; see the shell-dimples gap. The QSFP-DD lamps are arranged differently, as they are on every UfiSpace box: each 100G column carries four round lamps ABOVE it (green in the render, measured at x 375.1/379.1/383.1/387.1 and 393.8/397.8/401.8/405.8, a 4.0 mm pitch, in a strip that visibly interrupts the vent perforation) for its top-row port, and four BELOW it on the olive band for its bottom-row port. The 400G column has NO lamp row above it - the vent perforation runs unbroken across x 478-500 at the same rows - and two lamps below, at 418.2 and 426.2 mm. That asymmetry is measured, not assumed; what the lamps MEAN is nowhere stated, see the port-led-semantics gap.
provenance.port-media: THE PRINTED COLOUR BAND UNDER THE PORTS IS WHAT ASSIGNS THE MEDIA, and it is the one thing on this faceplate that a 520 px image reads unambiguously. Sampling the band per column gives twenty yellow columns (RGB 104,104,53), four teal (39,94,92), then olive (64,79,48) under two QSFP-DD columns and steel blue (56,93,118) under the last. That is exactly the datasheet's inventory - 40 x 1/10/25G SFP28, 8 x 1/10/25/50G SFP56, 4 x 100G QSFP-DD, 2 x 400G QSFP-DD - in the order the datasheet lists it, and it is what fixes which port is which.
provenance.port-numbers: THE FACEPLATE PRINTS THEM AND THIS RENDER CANNOT READ THEM. The yellow, teal and blue bands each carry two dark glyph clusters per column at 1.8-2.0 mm cap height, which is two pixels; the olive band carries none at all, which is a reading and not a miss - see the qsfp-100g-unnumbered gap for the side-by-side that establishes it. So the NUMERALS DRAWN HERE ARE A RECONSTRUCTION, not a transcription: 0-53 left to right, even along the top row and odd along the bottom, which is the numbering every UfiSpace box in this library uses (S7801-54XS 0-53 on the same 48+6 shape, S9610-36D 0-35, S9510-28DC) and which the up/down lamp pair in each column corroborates. Whether UfiSpace numbers the 400G pair first on this SKU is not knowable from any held document; see the port-numbering gap. The olive band's four ports are left unlabelled because nothing is printed there to label them with.
provenance.power: datasheet 'Typical power: 125 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. NO MAXIMUM IS PUBLISHED. The S9610-36D's HIG states its maximum four times over; this platform has no HIG, so there is no max figure to carry and none is invented. Inputs are the datasheet's: 100-240 V 10 A AC, -40 to -75 V 28 A DC. Each supply is 750 W from its own ordering line ('PSU-751-AESR-1C, 750W AC'). The fans publish no draw at all, so the L27/L29 warning stands and any total built from the modules is a floor.
provenance.rear-layout: ESTIMATED IN EVERY COORDINATE, and the inventory is the only sourced part. The datasheet gives 'Hot swappable, 1+1 redundant PSUs' and 'Hot swappable, 4+1 redundant Fans' with front-to-back airflow and names the orderable parts (PSU-751-AESR-1C / PSU-751-DESR-1C at 750 W, FAN-405636-HD), so five fan bays and two supply bays at the rear is a fact. WHERE THEY SIT IS NOT: UfiSpace publishes no rear render for this model and no installation guide, so there is no image and no drawing of this face anywhere in the intake. The five fans are laid left to right on an even 52.0 mm pitch from x 12.0 and the two supplies at the right, which is the arrangement every 1RU box in this library has and is a GUESS about this one. Nothing is drawn that a photograph would be needed to place - no grounding pad, no position legends, no vent field - because inventing those would be worse than leaving the face plain. See the rear-geometry gap.
provenance.rj45-and-unknowns: ONE RJ45 on this face, in a bright bezel measured at x 8.0-20.4, y 17.6-34.3 mm (12.4 wide x 16.7 tall) with a 9.8 x 13.2 mm opening. It is the ToD jack: the datasheet's Timing Interfaces row names a ToD input/output RJ45, it sits inside the timing block, and the three OTHER RJ45/USB connectors the datasheet lists are not on this face at all (see the rear-management-ports gap). No library RJ45 fits a 12.4 mm bezel - std/rj45 is 16.0 wide, common/rj45-shielded 15.8 - so std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) is placed on the measured width and centre with the bright bezel drawn as panel decor behind it, per the rule that a std/ port draws the opening and the metal shell around it is panel. The jack's LATCH DIRECTION IS NOT READABLE at 1.1 px/mm; it is drawn in the component's own orientation and the question is recorded. Three small dark circles on the left block are drawn because the render puts them there and are NOT named: one 2.7 mm at (6.2, 14.5) above the jack, which reads as a recessed reset button and is placed as common/reset-button on that reading, and two more at (6.2, 37.4) and (16.9, 37.4) below it, drawn as decor. A 4.4 mm round icon at (72.4, 5.7) between the model legend and the lamp tile is likewise drawn and unnamed. With no guide there is no callout list to resolve any of them.
provenance.sfp-layout: photo-measured, and THE PITCH WAS TAKEN FROM THE SHELL SEPARATORS, which repeat once per column, not from any filled module face. A local-maximum scan of the upper cage band finds 25 separators from x 41 to x 428 px at a uniform 16.125 px, which is 14.33 mm - the SFF-8433 ganged pitch of 14.25 to 0.6%, or 0.09 px per port. The standard pitch is therefore used and anchored at the measured left edge, and the check is what happens at the far end: twelve columns of 14.25 from 24.0 mm reach 195.0 against a measured shell break at 234.5 px (195.1 mm), and twelve more from the measured 197.3 reach 368.3 against a measured last separator at 428 px (368.0 mm). Two independent 171 mm runs landing within 0.3 mm is what says the pitch is right. Row pitch is measured at 17 px = 15.0 mm, which is std/sfp-ganged's own 15.00 belly-to-belly figure, so the two rows are placed on it exactly. The drawn dark aperture is only 9 px (7.9 mm) tall against the standard's 10.4 - that is the render's black area inside a grey wall, not a smaller cage - so the standard height is used, centred on the measured aperture centres at y 15.0 and 29.9 mm.
provenance.sources: UfiSpace S9620-54DC datasheet for dimensions, weight, the port inventory, platform, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; two vendor renders (photos/s9620-54dc-2-front, -1-angle) for everything else. THERE IS NO HARDWARE INSTALLATION GUIDE. UfiSpace has published none for the S9620 family, so this model has no faceplate figure, no callout list, no LED table, no FRU dimension table and no rear elevation - every one of which the S9610-36D and S7801-54XS models leaned on. What that costs is recorded feature by feature below and in the gaps register. THE DATASHEET SETS ITS SPEC TEXT AS OUTLINED GLYPHS: pdftotext returns 1471 bytes of bullet characters and headings, and the docling doc.md is the same headings with no values, so a reader who trusted either would conclude the vendor published nothing. The figures were recovered by rendering both pages at 200 and 1200 dpi with pdftocairo and reading them; every number in attrs comes off that render.
provenance.status-lamps: photo-measured and DELIBERATELY UNLABELLED. A dark recessed tile at x 78.2-105.5, y 2.6-8.8 mm carries six lamps: four green on the top row at x 79.6, 86.2, 92.9, 99.6 (y 4.4) and two on the bottom row (y 7.0), green at 79.6 and BLUE at 100.0. A printed legend sits beside each and is two pixels tall. The 4+2 shape with a blue lamp under the last of the four is the S7801-54XS's HIG-documented cluster exactly (SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 with ID beneath PS1), and the extra green lamp is where a timing box's SYNC would go - but that is a pattern match, not a reading, so NO LEGEND IS PRINTED HERE and the lamps carry positional ids. The blue lamp keeps a blue beacon state because its colour is measured. See the status-lamp-legends gap.
provenance.timing-block: photo-measured. Three round gold jacks across the top of the left block, isolated by colour: one 10.2 mm across centred at (12.9, 7.0) and two 8.0 mm at (29.3, 5.3) and (44.4, 5.3). The big one is the GNSS SMA - the datasheet's Timing Interfaces row lists exactly one SMA and two SMB, and an SMA nut is the larger - and the two small ones are the SMB pair. WHICH SMB IS WHICH IS NOT READ: a legend sits beside each jack and is four pixels tall. They are assigned 10MHz then 1PPS in the datasheet's own listing order, which is a convention and not a reading; see the smb-assignment gap. Construction follows the S9311-64D and S9610-36D: a gold decor disc for the knurled nut with the registry bore (std/sma, std/smb) on top, rather than common/smb-jack, which draws a hex nut this hardware does not have.
provenance.vent-islands: derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.
provenance.views: Six views, all with drawn content, and four of them estimated throughout. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention. The angle render shows three long shallow stiffening ribs running ACROSS the width (they are parallel to the front edge in the image, not to the side edge) and a scatter of small fastener dimples; the count is read from the render and the positions are spread evenly, estimated. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries a compliance sticker at an estimated position - no image shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT) each carry three countersunk ear-mount screws in a column near the front and four rail features along the length, both visible in the angle render's left side face and neither dimensioned anywhere. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by an asymmetric feature.
